W-01.note: register/rarity: two rare words (coeval, conjectural); conjectural is the one that fits an epistemic slot describing a claim, coeval needs a same-age comparison the other options do not presuppose

W-02.note: odd one out: cyclical/protracted/concentrated all describe how a process is distributed in TIME; reversible describes direction

W-03.note: two near-synonym pairs (halted/deferred, floating/hanging) cancel each other; no residual signal

W-04.note: collocation: only 'representative' idiomatically takes a sample/selection as subject; 'generous' is the evaluative odd one

W-05.note: hedging: uniform/recent/seasonal are categorical descriptors, modest is the qualified degree word these items tend to key

W-06.note: register: perceptible is the only technical detectability term; the other three are evaluative

W-07.note: no clean split; parallels chosen as the relation-between-two-things reading

W-08.note: dissolves/separates pair and settles/determines pair cancel; coin flip inside the second pair

W-09.note: specificity: 'verbatim transcripts' is the precise/technical phrase; the other three are vague document categories

W-10.note: collocation with evidence + odd one out: stratified/intermittent/provisional describe structure or timing, anecdotal evaluates evidentiary quality

W-11.note: sense-list item on 'economy': key is the non-dominant sense; 'a system of trade and finance' is the dominant one and therefore the trap

W-13.note: register: adjudicate is the technical/legal verb in a set of ordinary ones

W-14.note: degree hedging: verified/recorded pair and curbed/halted pair; within the live pair the partial term (curbed) is the qualified one

W-15.note: register: chronicle is the elevated verb among three plain ones

W-16.note: near-synonym pair framework/structure cannot hold a unique key, which halves the field to appearance/composition; composition is the substantive one

W-17.note: sense-list on 'temperate': 'mild in climate' is the dominant sense and so the trap; key is the moderate/restrained sense

W-18.note: odd one out: plentiful/essential/inherited are neutral, formulaic is the only evaluative-pejorative option

W-19.note: sense-list on 'homely': 'plain and unadorned' is the dominant US sense and therefore the trap; key is the less-familiar comfortable/inviting sense

W-20.note: literal/faithful are interchangeable in a translation frame so neither can be a unique key; idiomatic over exacting

W-21.note: hedging: justifies/disputes/certifies are strong stances, modifies is the qualified one

W-22.note: cross-item cluster: same target word as W-11/W-30/W-32 ('economy'); the sense fixed by the definition-format item selects frugality here

W-23.note: odd one out: curated/preserved/edited are custodial acts, staged alone implies artifice

W-25.note: sense-list on 'address': location of a residence is dominant and therefore the trap; key is the archaic 'adroitness' sense

W-26.note: register/rarity: dispositive is the one technical term among three ordinary academic words

W-28.note: non-dominant sense of a common word: 'schooled' = trained, the metaphorical reading these items favour

W-29.note: odd one out: discipline/bargaining/sabotage are social actions, insurance is the metaphorical hedge

W-30.note: same 'economy' cluster; frugality is blocked here because spareness is its near-synonym in a money-free (stylistic) frame, so spareness is the stylistic reading

W-31.note: sense-list on 'color': applying pigment is dominant and the trap; key is the figurative 'bias the impression of'

W-32.note: same 'economy' cluster; thrift is the sparing-use sense, commerce/system are the dominant-sense traps

W-33.note: register: circular is the technical logic term among three ordinary flaw words

W-34.note: sense-list: 'financial gains' is the dominant sense and the trap; gradual accumulations is the non-dominant one

W-35.note: hedging: provoke/harmonize/toughen are directional, moderate is the qualifying verb; also matches the temperate cluster

W-37.note: non-dominant sense: 'anticipated' = foreshadowed rather than expected

W-38.note: non-dominant sense: settle (a question) is the polysemous odd one among three concrete verbs

W-40.note: odd one out: concession/oversight/maneuver are all strategic or fault readings, 'a genuine prediction' is the only sincere one and is explicitly marked genuine

W-41.note: two options share the 'an act of X' frame; picked outside it but with no independent reason

W-44.note: register/abstraction: legitimize is the one abstract political verb among three concrete ones

W-45.note: sense-list on 'critical': decisive/essential are interchangeable so neither can be the unique key, leaving censorious/analytic; analytic is the sense these items test

W-49.note: non-dominant sense of a common word: 'arrest' = stop, matching the recurring channel in W-28/W-38/W-44

W-50.note: same 'temperate' cluster as W-17 in single-word format; 'mild in climate' and 'abstaining from alcohol' are the dictionary traps, measured is the W-17 sense
